subject: nodejs
question: Which Error constructor option stores an underlying error so it can be wrapped and inspected later?
options: { inner }
{ cause }
{ parent }
{ source }
explanation: new Error(message, { cause }) is available since Node.js 16.9 and is read back from error.cause.

subject: nodejs
question: When two CommonJS modules require each other, what does the module that loads second receive from the first?
options: The complete exports, because Node loads both at once
An error, since circular requires are not allowed
The partially filled exports object as it exists at that moment
undefined, always
explanation: The first module is still executing when the cycle is detected, so its exports may be incomplete.

subject: nodejs
question: What does new URL('https://x.io/p?a=1&a=2').searchParams.get('a') return?
options: null
explanation: get() returns the first value for a key; getAll() returns every value.

subject: nodejs
question: Which version range does "~1.4.2" allow?
options: Exactly 1.4.2
explanation: A tilde range allows patch updates only; a caret range also allows minor updates.

subject: nodejs
question: Why does this code not wait for each save() to finish before logging 'done'? items.forEach(async (item) => { await save(item); }); console.log('done');
options: console.log always runs before any promise settles
save() must return a value synchronously
await cannot be used inside arrow functions
forEach ignores the promises returned by its callbacks, so the loop does not wait
explanation: Use a for...of loop with await, or Promise.all() over items.map(), to wait for all the saves.

subject: nodejs
question: Why is exec('ls ' + userInput) riskier than spawn('ls', [userInput])?
options: spawn cannot accept user input at all
exec always runs as root
exec runs the string through a shell, so shell metacharacters in the input can inject commands
spawn blocks the event loop while the child runs
explanation: With an argument array and no shell, spawn passes the input as a single literal argument.

subject: nodejs
question: What advantage does stream.pipeline() have over chaining .pipe() calls?
options: It buffers the whole input in memory before writing
It forwards errors to one callback and destroys every stream in the chain when one fails
It disables backpressure so writes are faster
It runs each stream on its own thread
explanation: pipe() does not propagate errors or clean up the other streams automatically, which can leak resources.

subject: nodejs
question: Which event on a writable stream fires after end() has been called and all pending data has been flushed?
options: 'close'
'finish'
'end'
'drain'
explanation: 'finish' signals that all data has been handed to the underlying system; 'end' is a readable-side event.

subject: nodejs
question: Which kind of stream is meant to change data as it passes through, such as a gzip compressor?
options: Readable
Writable
Transform
Server
explanation: A Transform is a Duplex stream whose output is computed from its input.

subject: nodejs
question: What is the usual pattern for a graceful shutdown of an HTTP server on SIGTERM?
options: Call process.abort() right away
Send SIGKILL to the process ID
Ignore the signal because SIGTERM cannot be caught
Call server.close() and let in-flight requests finish before exiting
explanation: SIGTERM can be handled with process.on('SIGTERM'), which lets the server drain before the process exits.
